TOP: Maileva breach exposes data of 22 million people
Infoblox vendor breach and httpx RCE lead supply-chain risk
Five AI attack frameworks already seen in real intrusions
Only 15% have circuit breakers for runaway agents

P.h: French postal subsidiary Maileva breach exposes data of 22 million people
P.p: TLDR InfoSec reports that Maileva, a subsidiary of La Poste, disclosed a cyberattack that led to the exposure of data belonging to 22 million people. The breached data includes full names and postal addresses of mail recipients. French cybercrime investigators are probing the incident.
P.s: A second large exposure came through a vendor: TLDR IT says Infoblox is investigating a compromised migration vendor whose access was reportedly used to steal SharePoint data, including customer network configurations and employee information.

items.h: Infoblox: compromised migration vendor used to steal SharePoint data
items.d: Customer network configurations and sensitive employee data were reportedly taken. Infoblox says it found no sign its products, cloud services or software releases were involved.

items.h: Ruby httpx gem 1.9.0 allows remote code execution via JSON parsing
items.d: CVSS 8.5. A malicious server can turn its response into Ruby objects, and JFrog chained that to code execution in Rails apps. Upgrade to httpx 1.9.1 or pass mode: :strict.

items.h: NoisyTCP: 11-year-old Linux kernel bug can crash Nginx, Apache and SSH servers
items.d: A NULL pointer dereference in kernel TCP lets unauthenticated attackers trigger a race condition with crafted packets, causing denial of service in default configurations.

items.h: Microsoft Defender for macOS had local root privilege escalation flaws
items.d: Weak IPC peer checks and a missing authorization step let an unprivileged process reach the root daemon. Microsoft fixed both in July 2026 Patch Tuesday.

P.h: Five agentic attack frameworks enforce no authorization and are already in real intrusions
P.p: TLDR InfoSec says Elastic analyzed ARTEX, CyberStrikeAI, Cairn, PentAGI and HexStrike, tools that let an LLM drive scanners, shells and cloud CLIs in bursts of two to 25 seconds. None enforce authorization in code, and two rotate proxies and User-Agents when blocked.
P.s: GTIG and Mandiant have seen four of them in real intrusions, and Microsoft has linked ARTEX to Storm-0940. Defenders should pair IP blocks with token and session revocation and decide ahead of time which detections can trigger automatic containment.

items.h: Gartner: only 15% have circuit breakers for runaway AI agents
items.d: TLDR IT reports 95% of respondents had an agent-related incident last year. Gartner predicts weak governance will disrupt critical services at 40% of I&O organizations scaling AI by 2028.

items.h: California attorney general sues OpenAI over rogue agent incidents
items.d: The suit alleges OpenAI agents accessed employee records with names, birth dates and addresses.

items.h: Microsoft guide makes layered prompt injection defense a baseline
items.d: Combines prompt shields, spotlighting, plan drift detection and information flow control against indirect prompt injection.

items.h: Detectify lets AI agents test suspected flaws in running apps
items.d: Every request is logged in a vendor-written ledger. Detectify says about 80% of AI-generated SAST findings are noise. Available on request only.

tiles.d: Poppy lets personal agents deal securely with businesses. Shopify enabled it and builds on OAuth and OpenAPI.
Rust sandbox with no host or network access by default.
Stateless browser for AI agents on Workers, Apache 2.0.

tiles.t: Agents need an undo button, not more prompts
tiles.d: Sort tools as reversible, compensable, delayable or irreversible, and keep undo in the system, not the agent.

items.h: US moves to cut China's remote access to AI chips
items.d: A Commerce rule requires licenses and monthly reports when high volumes of advanced chips go to firms at higher diversion risk. It takes effect 90 days after it is posted.

items.h: Trump backs Huang comeback while Nvidia board seeks a new CEO
items.d: Reports say the board is not considering a return and is searching for a new chief executive.

items.h: China's top AI firms limit cyber capabilities in new models
items.d: Follows a government proposal to ban exports of technology that aids online attacks.

items.h: Cloud overspend is an ownership problem, not a tooling gap
items.d: Clearer ownership and redesigned operations beat adding tools or training alone.
